code: espeak_Synth((char*) str, size + 1, 0, POS_CHARACTER, 0, synth_flags, NULL, NULL);
note: Fuzzer input bytes are passed as UTF-8 text with espeakSSML flag, entering the SSML parser.
Local stack buffer of 501 wchar_t elements (N_XML_BUF=500) that receives the SSML tag content.

code: while (!Eof() && (c1 != '>') && (n_xml_buf < N_XML_BUF)) { xml_buf[n_xml_buf++] = c1; c1 = GetC(); }
note: Tag characters are read into xml_buf until '>' or buffer limit; xml_buf[n_xml_buf]=0 terminates the string.
The parsed tag buffer is passed to ProcessSsmlTag for SSML tag handling.

code: len = wcslen(xml_buf); if (xml_buf[len - 1] == '/') { xml_buf[len - 1] = ' '; self_closing = true; }
note: If the tag ends with '/', the last character is replaced with a space to mark self-closing.

code: for (ix = 0; ix < (sizeof(tag_name)-1); ix++) { if (((c = xml_buf[ix]) == 0) || iswspace(c)) break; tag_name[ix] = tolower((char)c); }
note: Tag name is parsed from xml_buf; ix stops at the first space or null, and px is set to &xml_buf[ix].
px points to the position in xml_buf after the tag name, which is where attributes begin.
GetSsmlAttribute reads pw[-1] (one wchar_t before the pointer) to check for whitespace; if pw points to &xml_buf[0], this reads 4 bytes before the stack buffer, causing a stack-buffer-overflow READ.
GetVoiceAttributes is called with px from ProcessSsmlTag; it calls GetSsmlAttribute(pw,...) where pw=px, propagating the out-of-bounds read when px points to the start of xml_buf.
The tag type is determined; for a closing tag like </speak>, tag_type becomes SSML_CLOSE|SSML_SPEAK, causing GetVoiceAttributes to be invoked with px.
When pw points to &xml_buf[0] (ix==0), pw[-1] reads 4 bytes before the xml_buf stack array, triggering ASAN stack-buffer-overflow READ of 1 wchar_t.
